title: AI Impacts, Trends & Strategy + Project Demos
description:
This session examines where AI is genuinely reshaping industries, what that means for the future, and for students entering the workforce.

The focus will be lean towards IT and software engineering disciplines but the trends here directly impact other key industries as well.

We’ll cover-

* The current state of applied AI and where the immediate impacts are
* Crucial trends that are reshaping industries
* Structural disruption v. cosmetic impacts
* Opportunities & risks to watch for
* Skills & mindset shifts to focus on developing
* Why AI is a moving target and how to mitigate the unknowns

I'm going to structure this session specially-

1. Initial Q&A, bring your questions, challenges and concerns about AI and how it's affecting your industry
2. One hour focus presentation on crucial trends, what to watch, and why it matters
3. Discussion Q&A after the presentation
4. Project demonstrations - we'll look at some live projects built with AI and utilizing AI to frame the discussions of where AI is having the greatest immediate impact

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Using Copilot for Design and Actions Workflows
description:
We are back for another edition of the GitHub User Group. This month we dive into using Copilot and AI to enhance the design workflow, and look at how we can leverage AI in our GitHub Actions.

**Product Design with Source Control: Using GitHub, AI, and Preview Builds as Your Source of Truth \~ [Walt Lim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/waltzaround/)**

In this talk, Walt shares how he uses GitHub and AI to rethink the design process, moving beyond traditional prototypes to code as the source of truth. By using pull requests and ephemeral preview builds, he creates fast, realistic, and testable environments where ideas can be reviewed, iterated, and validated in context. Combined with AI-assisted workflows, this approach helps his team move quicker, reduce ambiguity, and make better decisions with less overhead

**From One PR to Another: Agentic Workflows on GitHub \~ [Sinan Nar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sinannar/)**

A live demo of using AI-driven workflows to trigger actions across repositories—automatically creating a PR in a second repo when changes are merged.
bio: Sinan is an Apps and AI Consultant at ARINCO, a Microsoft and GitHub partner consultancy. He co-organises the Aotearoa Azure User Group and the Auckland .NET User Group. An experienced and certified software engineer, he specialises in the Microsoft ecosystem, with a focus on Azure and GitHub.

title: Film Screening | The Second Interrogation
location: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki, Wellesley Street East, Auckland City Centre, Auckland
description:
Join us for a screening of The Second Interrogation by artist Wang Tuo, followed by a conversation with Hutch Wilco, curator of Forever Tomorrow: Chinese Art Now.
The event will begin with a brief introduction to the film from Hutch, offering curatorial context and insight into the work. After the screening, you are warmly invited to stay for questions and a kōrero with Hutch.
The Second Interrogation (2023) explores systems of power, censorship and psychological control in contemporary China. Staged as an intense encounter between an artist and a cultural censor, the film unfolds through dialogue, repetition and role reversal, gradually blurring the boundaries between authority and resistance. Drawing on historical reference points and lived experience, the work examines how ideology operates through language, surveillance and self-regulation, while asking urgent questions about the role of art today.
This screening offers an opportunity to engage with key themes in Forever Tomorrow and to reflect collectively on the film’s social, political and artistic resonances.
Please note the film is in Mandarin Chinese with English subtitles. The kōrero with Hutch will be in English.
About Hutch:/
H E Wilco is a curator, writer and exhibition developer with nearly three decades of experience delivering major museum projects in New Zealand and China. Based in Shanghai for almost a decade, he worked in the city’s private art sector before founding an exhibition development practice specialising in curatorial research and exhibition strategy. He has curated exhibitions for leading museums and galleries across China, with a particular focus on post-1980s Chinese artists, and writes regularly for international arts publications.

title: Craft a puppet creature
location: Botany Library, 588 Chapel Road, East Tāmaki, Auckland 2013, Auckland
description:
Join artist Sarah Cowie and get creative in this beginner-friendly puppet-making workshop, great for kids 8+, adults, and families!
Get creative in this fun, hands-on puppet-making workshop run by artist Sarah Cowie where fabric comes to life! Participants will transform soft materials into playful puppet creatures using simple, easy-to-learn techniques. With fabric, string, beads, ribbon, and decorative elements, you’ll design and shape a unique character inspired by Sarah's own puppet creations. Add a rod controller and watch your creature become a fully performable puppet!
Along the way, you’ll learn how to create shape and form from fabric, develop personality and character, and pick up basic hand-sewing skills, no experience needed. A selection of the artist’s puppets will be on display to spark ideas and imagination.
Once your puppet is complete, step behind a theatre-style backdrop to bring it to life! Perform, play, and snap photos of your creation in action.
This beginner-friendly workshop is perfect for children 8+, adults looking to experiment with fun materials, and families, offering an exciting opportunity to experiment with new materials, try something different, and build confidence in your creativity. You’ll leave with a one-of-a-kind puppet and a big sense of achievement.
All materials are provided.
The project is funded by Arts Out East, a programme of Te Tuhi supported by the Howick Local Board.

description:
It is time to swap until you drop. Refresh the whole whānau wardrobe, as this year the whole house will be a swap shop! 
Get your tokens from dropping clothing to us in the weeks leading up to the event. Then use those tokens to swap until your heart is content!
Drop-off | Weekdays from Monday 13 April, 9am-3pm
Clothing must be good quality and in good condition.
We're accepting kid, teen and adult items (up to 15 items).
Get up to 10 tokens to use on the Swap Shop Day.
​We will not be able to accept donations outside drop-off times.
On the day | Sunday 3 May, 10am-1pm
Use one token per item. 
Want extra items? Just $5 each. 
Cash is brilliant - bring it! We will have an Eftpos machine but to speed up the lines and get you in quicker, bring your cash.
Enjoy Chiasso filter coffee to fuel your swap frenzy.
